title: HyperPatch: Sequential Knowledge Editing Under N-ary Structural Drift

problem.claim: Sequential knowledge editing must maintain temporal validity for inherently n-ary real-world knowledge in non-stationary environments.

gap.claim: Binary reification of n-ary events into triples can fracture relational atomicity, causing structural drift and structure-conditioned knowledge transfer failure that may be misdiagnosed as parametric hallucination.

contributions.claim: HyperPatch reformulates sequential knowledge editing as a stability problem over hypergraph manifolds while preserving model parameters.
HyperPatch combines topology-aware initialization, sequential topology editing, and structure-conditioned reasoning to preserve event integrity during n-ary updates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the MQuAKE-CF and MQuAKE-T benchmarks, HyperPatch achieves relative Hop-wise Accuracy gains of 96.24% and 21.06%, respectively, over the strongest baseline.
Ablation results reportedly show superior reliability under continuous n-ary update streams, while the standard KG-based variant exhibits Hop-wise Accuracy collapses of up to 88.3%.
The authors report that the code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge editing is used to maintain temporal validity, but real-world knowledge is n-ary.
Sequential updates to complex relations can produce structural drift and knowledge transfer failure.
HyperPatch addresses the problem by treating sequential editing as a hypergraph-manifold stability problem.
The framework uses topology-aware initialization, dual-stage topology editing, and structure-conditioned reasoning.
The authors report benchmark gains and improved reliability under continuous n-ary updates.

source_observation.claim: Representing n-ary events as binary triples can fracture relational atomicity and induce structural misalignment.

interpretation.claim: Knowledge-editing systems may require structure-preserving representations when updates involve high-order relations.

application.claim: For sequential updates to complex relations, evaluate whether the representation preserves event-level structure rather than only individual binary facts.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that hypergraph-based editing is necessary or superior for tasks whose relations are intrinsically binary.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, baselines, absolute accuracy values, or statistical significance.
The abstract does not provide implementation details sufficient to assess reproducibility or computational cost.
The abstract does not independently verify the reported benchmark gains or ablation results.
